statement: Show that for all \(x > 1\) there exists a triangle with sides \(x^4+x^3+2x^2+x+1\), \(2x^3+x^2+2x+1\), and \(x^4-1\).

Find all real numbers \(a, b, c\) such that \(x^3 + ax^2 + bx + c\) has three real roots \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) (not necessarily distinct) and the equation \(x^3 + \alpha^3 x^2 + \beta^3 x + \gamma^3\) has roots \(\alpha^3, \beta^3, \gamma^3\).
Triangle \(ABC\) is given. Find a point \(X\) on \(BC\) such that \(\dfrac{[ABX]}{[ACX]} = \dfrac{\text{perimeter of } \triangle ABX}{\text{perimeter of } \triangle ACX}\).
For each integer \(n > 0\), show that there exists a polynomial \(p(x)\) such that \(p(2\cos x) = 2\cos nx\).
Find all real numbers \(k\) such that \(x^2 - 2x\lfloor x \rfloor + x - k = 0\) has at least two non-negative roots.

\(ABCD\) is a rectangle with \(BC/AB = \sqrt{2}\). \(ABEF\) is a congruent rectangle in a different plane. Find angle \(DAF\) such that lines \(CA\) and \(BF\) are perpendicular. In this configuration, find two points on \(CA\) and two on \(BF\) forming a regular tetrahedron.
